A1.justification: Both PDFs contain the same research work, Differential Coding for Training-Free ANN-to-SNN Conversion. All 30 pages in each version, including Appendices A–P, are readable and support comparison of text, equations, figures and tables.

before.justification: v2 reports original ImageNet conversion experiments and ablations in Section 5 and Appendices K–M, plus COCO object-detection and PascalVOC segmentation results in Appendices N–O.

after.justification: v3 retains the original ImageNet, COCO and PascalVOC experiments, including numerical accuracy, energy estimates and ablation results in Tables 1–10.

M1.justification: The differential coding procedure, graded units, spiking neurons, threshold iteration and Algorithms 1–3 are unchanged. Equations (14) and (37) reorder equivalent expressions without changing the update rule.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate ImageNet classification, COCO object detection and PascalVOC semantic segmentation. No dataset, task, domain or test scenario is added or removed.

E2.justification: Table 2 retains TS, SNM, MMSE, QCFS, SRP, MST, STA, SpikeZIP-TF and ECMT. The rate-coding and 99.9% large-activation comparators also remain unchanged in the corresponding ablations.

E3.justification: The reported architectures, time-step grids, threshold numbers and scales, evaluation metrics and energy-estimation assumptions are unchanged. No new evaluation protocol is introduced.

E4.justification: Sections 5.3–5.4 and Appendices L–O retain the same differential-versus-rate-coding and threshold-selection ablations. No robustness, sensitivity, error-analysis or case-study evidence is added or removed.

E5.justification: The experimental results retain the same point-estimate reporting. Neither version reports experimental run or seed counts, uncertainty intervals or significance tests.

E6.justification: Tables 1–10 and the plotted findings are unchanged. For example, Table 1 retains VGG16-4/1 accuracy of 73.17% and energy ratio 0.22 at T=8. Figure 2 retains the same curves despite revised labels.

T1.justification: Appendix B replaces Equation (38)'s valid summation-to-recurrence derivation with a reverse recursive expansion. The new fourth displayed line drops the factor (t-1)/t when expanding r^l[t-1], incorrectly leaving denominators t-1 instead of t in the last two terms. This introduces a localized algebraic error; the underlying identity and other theoretical content are unchanged.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction contributions and conclusion retain the same claims about training-free conversion, differential coding, threshold optimization, hardware implementation, accuracy and energy efficiency.

C2.justification: The mechanism explanations and limitations remain unchanged, including the need for negative thresholds and the lack of optimal threshold selection for Transformers. Figure 2's revised labels clarify its already-stated ideal-fitting interpretation.

D1.justification: The threshold-setting instructions, hardware discussion, GPU implementation in Appendix P and code-access link are unchanged. No implementation or reproducibility information is added or removed.

R1.justification: Section 2, the references and the positioning relative to earlier conversion methods are unchanged. No cited work or novelty claim is added or removed.

P1.justification: v3 updates the version/date banner, revises Figure 2 terminology and locally reworks Appendix B's exposition. Equations (14) and (37) foreground the recurrence; the wider prose and section organization remain unchanged.

P2.justification: Figure 2 changes its axes from encoded input/output to Ideal Encoded Value and Closest Encoded Value while retaining its curves and scale. The longer Equation (38) causes limited reflow across pages 13–15; no figure or table is added or removed.

improvement.justification: Figure 2's clearer labels provide a small presentation benefit, but Appendix B introduces a false intermediate equality into a previously valid derivation. With the underlying method, identity and empirical evidence unchanged, this constitutes a localized decline in mathematical reliability rather than a broader loss of scientific substance.
